name: W Montreal
positioning: A design-driven W hotel on Square Victoria in the old Banque du Canada building, between Old Montreal and downtown, with Montreal-inspired penthouse suites and a music-led bar scene
best_for: Design and music lovers who want penthouse suites with Montreal stories built in
City-breakers who want Old Montreal and downtown both within walking reach

facts.text: The Old Port's landmarks, waterfront experiences and restaurants are within a 10-minute walk of the hotel.
To the left of the hotel are the Old Port and Notre Dame Basilica.
The Bell Centre is a 10-minute walk from the hotel.
The hotel sits above a Metro station whose entrance has a classic Art Nouveau sign.
The Premium Penthouse Suite has a library inspired by Montreal's Villa Maria metro station.
The Penthouse King Suite's island unit draws inspiration from the Biosphere, the Palais des Congres and Habitat 67.
The Penthouse II Suite is spread over two stories.
Each Penthouse Suite has a private terrace with views of downtown Montreal.
The Retro Gaming Box offers a lineup of classic video game consoles.
The Living Room is a coworking space by day that turns into a bar when the day is done.
Tbsp. is the hotel's restaurant, combining French and Italian flavors in dishes made for sharing.
Pet services include dog walking, grooming and pet birthday cakes, at an additional cost.

highlights.text: The hotel is on Square Victoria inside the old Banque du Canada building.
The hotel has a foot in historic Old Montreal and a finger on the pulse of the downtown scene.
The Penthouse Corner Suite has ribbons suspended above the bed in homage to Cirque du Soleil, and the largest terrace at W Montreal.
The Vinyl Bar has a curated collection of 3,000 records, a custom listening station and live DJ sets.
Bota Bota, a floating spa in Montreal's Old Port, is a short stroll from the hotel.

considerations.text: Conde Nast Traveler notes that, as with many W Hotels, late-night noise can be an issue.
Conde Nast Traveler has heard the atrium-view rooms can get a little dark, while park-facing rooms flood with natural light.
Conde Nast Traveler says the hotel is in a business district, not exactly in the middle of the action, but a five-minute walk from it.
